assessment.summary: Incomplete implementation — The new Paused state can be entered but is not integrated into the public state representation or any path that can leave it.

positives.summary: The transition rejects invalid source states before mutation.

findings.title: Incomplete paused-state lifecycle
findings.summary: Jobs can enter Paused, but the API reports that state as unknown and resumable never recognizes it.
findings.whyItMatters: A new domain state must be handled across every boundary and supported transition. A successful pause leaves callers with a state the public API cannot represent or recover from.
findings.impact: A successful pause leaves callers with a state the public API cannot represent or recover from.

evidence.message: The API falls through to unknown for the new state.
The resumable decision is hard-coded false for every state.
The pause operation transitions a running job into Paused.

findings.recommendation: Define the intended paused lifecycle, map Paused explicitly at the API boundary, implement its supported transition, and validate the round trip. If resume is intentionally deferred, reject pause in this release or expose the limitation explicitly instead of creating a terminal state accidentally.

metadata.principle: A new domain state must be handled across every boundary and supported transition.
metadata.tradeoffs: If resume is intentionally deferred, reject pause in this release or expose the limitation explicitly instead of creating a terminal state accidentally.

findings.title: Defective nil-guard on configuration spec
findings.summary: set_version_vulnerable only calls init_config under the condition that spec is already absent, leaving the initialization contract incomplete.
findings.whyItMatters: Initialization contracts for core config objects must be enforced on all paths before use; a guard that only activates when the field is already nil does not protect callers. Callers relying on the guard may observe uninitialized or partially initialized specs on some paths.
findings.impact: Callers relying on the guard may observe uninitialized or partially initialized specs on some paths.

evidence.message: init_config itself only populates inside the same nil check.
The vulnerable setter guards the init call on spec being none.

findings.recommendation: Make init_config unconditional from all public setters (as in set_version_clean) or remove the redundant outer guard so the helper always ensures a non-nil spec. If lazy init is intentional, callers must still guarantee the field before any use that assumes it is present.

metadata.principle: Initialization contracts for core config objects must be enforced on all paths before use; a guard that only activates when the field is already nil does not protect callers.
metadata.tradeoffs: If lazy init is intentional, callers must still guarantee the field before any use that assumes it is present.

findings.title: Missing paused-state boundary validation
findings.summary: The test proves that pause mutates the enum but does not exercise how the new state is presented or recovered.
findings.whyItMatters: Validation should cover the externally observable behavior and the risky state transition, not only the local assignment. The incomplete API integration can pass while the local transition test remains green.
findings.impact: The incomplete API integration can pass while the local transition test remains green.

evidence.message: The only test ends after checking the internal enum value.

findings.recommendation: Add a scenario that pauses a running job and verifies the public state plus the intended next transition. One lifecycle-level scenario is more valuable here than exhaustive unit cases for each match arm.

metadata.principle: Validation should cover the externally observable behavior and the risky state transition, not only the local assignment.
